body: I like this suggestion. Would it fit with other errors to say `The "export" keyword` and `Use the "@export" annotation`? I feel like that'd be a bit more grammatically correct, but I also remember other errors shortening sentences this way.

Note that there is more than one export annotation (not just `@export`, but also `@export_range`, `@export_enum`, etc.). But in this case, using `@` is appropriate, since otherwise it becomes more confusing. Maybe something like `The "export" keyword was removed in Godot 4. Use an export annotation instead ("@export", "@export_range", etc.).`?

`slave` and `sync` were deprecated ages ago (with `slave` being a controversial keyword), so I'd prefer not to bring them back in our codebase seemingly forever.

I don't think upgrading from Godot 3.0 to 4.5 directly is a supported use case :D
Makes sense. I'll remove those shortly! 🙂
